summary: 1935 CCC-built 100-ft steel fire tower in the Stanislaus NF; a 2019 NHLR visit calls it abandoned and unsafe, gated; FFLA still lists it standing.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower with a 7 by 7 foot cab; Aeromotor design per Peakbagging.com
facts.status_note: Listed as standing, but the January 2019 register visit calls it abandoned and unsafe

access.note: Access is gated; NHLR says only Forest Service staff and repeater-site representatives are allowed

visit.trail_note: Gated; the 2019 visit report calls the tower unsafe. The sources read describe no public route.

events.note: Built by CCC workers; NHLR and Peakbagging.com both date it to 1935

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR description calls the BC-2 residence still in use, but the 2019 visit report says it was severely vandalized and burned. The story follows the dated 2019 report and no longer says a residence stands beside the tower.

The 2019 visit report says the lookout has not been staffed for over a decade. Peakbagging.com, which gives no date, says it is in good condition and may be staffed during fire hazard periods. The story reports the dated 2019 finding as the latest record and gives Peakbagging.com's undated claims with that caveat.

notes_for_editor: The newest dated source is the January 2019 NHLR visit report, so today's condition is unknown. Peakbagging.com is undated apart from a 2011 photo credit; its 'in good condition' statement conflicts with the 2019 visit and is reported with that caveat. The FFLA standing listing is also undated. Waymarking pages returned no readable text and were not used. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced with 'closed' (gated). The brief's 'standing' status holds, with a status note about the 2019 condition.
